findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - an upgrade has landed on the default branch while an open fix still pins v1.2.42. The pinned close calls `_synced` before reaching either bridged wait; v1.2.42:src/forge/close.py:824-831 refuses because the default branch has a newer pin and tells the user to merge it. Wrapping only the checks functions leaves that refusal in place, so close never reaches the installed CI recovery without the pin upgrade this fix is meant to avoid.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - Forge is installed newer than a v1.2.42 branch, and close saves its review while the code-head CI run is still active. The released v1.2.42 checks module has no `after_code_ci`, and its close pushes the review record directly at v1.2.42:src/forge/close.py:429. This `hasattr` guard therefore skips the installed pre-push wait entirely. The push cancels the code's running CI instead of letting its retry finish and reuse its result. The test fixture supplies a hook that the actual release does not have.
findings.title: Functional: Run the pre-push CI wait for releases without its hook

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - an existing branch and default branch still pin v1.2.2 after the user installs a newer Forge. That release's `checks.wait` accepts only `top`, `item`, `sha` and `names` (v1.2.2:src/forge/checks.py:25), so binding its arguments produces no `branch`. The installed `checks.wait` requires that keyword (src/forge/checks.py:72-73), and the call in `serve` raises `TypeError` instead of waiting for CI. The branch can no longer close through this path.
findings.title: Functional: Supply the branch for older pinned wait signatures

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a user starts `forge land --all` from an older pinned checkout while the default branch still has that pin. The patch replaces `checks.wait` only in the current process. The released queue starts each item with a fresh interpreter and imports the pinned package again (v1.2.42:src/forge/land.py:825-831); its pin check sees the matching old version, so the child uses the old wait and treats a cancelled group as failed. The same loss occurs if a running v1.2.40 close merges a default branch pinned to v1.2.42: that release's `resume_pin` starts the intermediate release through its own unbridged `run_release` (v1.2.40:src/forge/repo.py:1017-1039). Both paths lose the newer recovery even though the installed release is newer.
findings.title: Functional: Preserve the CI bridge across pinned subprocesses

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a repo upgrades while an older branch remains open. The named proof sets the default branch to v1.2.42 and never advances it after creating the worktree. It also copies the current `close.py` into the supposed older package and replaces only `checks.py`, then asserts a rerun occurred without checking whether it finished before the review-record push. It therefore passes despite the actual v1.2.42 post-upgrade refusal and would pass if the pre-push bridge were removed but the final wait still retried. The named proof does not establish those promised behaviors.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_ci_wait_uses_newer_installed_release.py::test_1_pinned_commands_use_newer_ci_recovery_and_keep_pinned_review

why: A branch pinned to the earlier release runs close and merge through that release, so CI-wait fixes in a newer installed release (rerun failed groups, cancelled is not failed) do not apply until each branch merges the pin upgrade
